as_told.title: Rumsfeld's $2.3 trillion in unaccounted Pentagon spending

plain: The day before the September 11 attacks in 2001, Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld is said to have admitted publicly that the Pentagon could not account for trillions of dollars. The journalist Ross Coulthart says he dug up Rumsfeld's own speech while writing his book, and that in it Rumsfeld "admitted that there was something" wrong with the money. The researcher Richard Dolan tells it too, working from Pentagon records and the reporting of others. He says the figure was first "2.3 trillion dollars in unaccounted expenditures" and kept being revised. Dolan places the accounting before the House committee that oversees the military over 2001 and 2002, and credits Dov Zakheim and Catherine Austin Fitts, people who dealt with or wrote about the missing money. The tellers raise it because hidden money of that size could, in their view, fund secret programs, including UFO work, out of sight of Congress.
